text:
mira: Quick a11y check after the shortcuts overlay and filter pill updates. Saw three small issues: shortcut overlay not reachable via keyboard focus, filter pill counts low contrast in dark theme, and announcements duplicating when multiple filters applied. Posting summary.

owen: Repro steps? I can try locally.

mira: On staging: press ? to open shortcuts overlay. It appears but initial keyboard focus is inside the overlay only if you click it, not when opened via keyboard. Expected focus to land on the overlay close button or first shortcut item.

sasha: I can repro. Also the small numeric badge on pills uses #9A9A9A on dark card (#0E1013) — fails AA.

-dev-a11y-bot: Auto-check hints: (1) overlays should trap focus and set initial focus to the first focusable element; (2) badges need contrast >=4.5:1 for 12px normal text; (3) avoid multiple aria-live regions for filter updates.

owen: Proposed fixes: on overlay open call overlayEl.focus() and set aria-modal="true" role="dialog"; add focus trap while overlay open. For pills: update token chip-badge to #D1D5D9 in dark. For announcements: centralize to a single aria-live region and batch updates like "3 filters applied".

mira: Also small SR copy nit: when applying filters VoiceOver reads "Filter applied filter" sometimes because the pill has visible label and aria-label. Remove duplicate aria-labels and use aria-pressed for toggle state only when appropriate.

sasha: Validation plan: keyboard-only overlay open/close, focus trap works, pill contrast in both themes, VO/NVDA reads single batched announcement when filters change. I'll test after PR.

owen: I'll implement: focus on open, focus trap util, token bump for badge, and single live region util. Will tag @sasha.

mira: Thanks 44D. Acceptance checklist to paste into PR: open via keyboard, initial focus inside overlay, Esc closes and restores focus to previous control, pill badges meet contrast in dark/light, filter announcements are single and accurate.

dev-a11y-bot: Post-PR automation: run contrast and live-region checks.

sasha: Great 44C. Ping when ready and I'll run the SR matrix.
